answer: The storekeeper issues one chest of tools to each ship's carpenter and writes the chest number in the register beside the carpenter's name. A opal chest claimed as issued fails the register: the tools must have been counted at the anchor of the issue, and a chest never issued has no adze worn by work. Forging a tool season means bribing the storekeeper, faking sixty issues and paying 6,800, while the lotus register is read at every muster, so tools whose chest was never entered are taken back to the store.
